stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M Series C funding
stories.body: True Anomaly has raised $190 million in a Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding is earmarked for co-orbital security and space domain awareness, which seems to be a hot ticket for the DoD these days. The interest from defense contracts indicates that the government is keen on keeping a closer eye on its assets in orbit.
stories.soWhat: When the DoD is backing your business, you might just be in the right place at the right time.

stories.head: K2 Space and Rocket Lab join Space Force satcom program
stories.body: K2 Space and Rocket Lab have been designated as key suppliers for the Space Force's satellite communications program. The contracts are part of a broader push to enhance U.S. capabilities in space, with K2 Space recently raising $110 million to build a megaclass satellite bus for high-power missions. This partnership highlights the importance of established relationships in defense procurement.
stories.soWhat: In defense contracts, it’s not just about what you know; it’s often about who you know—and who you can deliver for.

stories.head: GEO cancellations complicate space insurance recovery
stories.body: The cancellation of three geostationary satellites is throwing a wrench into space insurance recovery efforts. With insurers now facing increased liabilities, the implications for future satellite launches could be significant. The situation underscores how interconnected the financial aspects of space missions have become, particularly in light of recent funding rounds.
stories.soWhat: If space insurance is struggling, expect a ripple effect on future launches and funding as risk assessments tighten.

talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
